newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister prefers moderate 7pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister prefers moderate 7pct growth.

text.p: Thailand's acting finance minister Chaiywat Wibulsawat said on Friday he would like to see the nation's economy grow by only about seven percent a year over the next five years to avoid further economic problems.
"I prefer to see the economy grow at the average of seven percent over the next five years. This will be a sustainable growth and create economic stability," Chaiyawat told a seminar.
"We should no longer expect to have double digit economic growth," he said. "High growth can sometimes create many economic problems."

Over the past five years Thailand has averaged 8.5 percent gross domestic product aPLGDP (GDP) growth -- a figure Chaiyawat said was among the highest in the world. This year private economists predict GDP to grow by less than 7.0 percent.
"High economic growth caused rising imports of capital goods and raw materials. This has added pressure on the current account deficit and trade deficit," he said.
Chaiywat said the finance ministry is conducting a four to five year plan to reduce the current account deficit to about four to five percent of GDP.
Thailand's current account deficit widened to 8.1 percent of GDP at the end of 1995 compared with 5.6 percent in the previous year, he said.
"The C/A deficit is the major problem we have to tackle. But we don't want to reduce it too quickly," Chaiyawat said.

He said one of the finance ministry's measures to reduce the deficit is to boost domestic long-term savings such as pension and provident funds in order to narrow the gap between domestic investments and savings.

"Thailand's domestic savings of more than 30 percent of GDP are very high compared with other countries," he said. "But it remains low as the country's domestic investment is at about 40 percent of GDP."
Chaiyawat said the slow export growth will adversely affect he country's economic growth which had mainly been driven by exports
"We have to quickly solve the export problem if we want to maintain our robust economic growth," he said.

Thai exports grew by about 3.2 percent in the first eight months compared with growth of a 23.6 percent for all of 1995. Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan said recently that Thai exports for all of 1996 will not grow more than 5.0 percent.
